rationale: Both candidates independently found the live ground-truth blocker — the async engine hardcodes rel_l1_thresh=0.2, silencing the MiniMax-H3 model-specific 0.17 default — with equally rigorous code-path tracing and concrete fixes. X goes further: it explicitly verifies the partition/combined-pipeline gating (echoing GT concern #1) and independently surfaces that the E2E smoke test never asserts a real cache hit, nearly verbatim matching the human reviewer's own caveat ('does not assert that real denoising produces a cache hit'). X's extra findings (coefficient near-constancy/non-monotonicity, memory retention, eager RoPE, test staleness) show deeper investigative rigor mirroring the GT reviewer's own use of the PR's evaluation data. Y's supplementary findings (doc/help-text default mismatches, warning wording) are valid but more surface-level and less aligned with GT themes. Both are well-grounded and actionable with specific file/line fixes, but X's recall and depth edge out Y.
